system_description.narrative_title: Energy shocks, geopolitical brinkmanship and financial strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where Middle East security shocks and unconventional warfare are disrupting energy flows and transport, prompting ad hoc political bargains over fuel supplies. Those supply shocks are amplifying inflation and bond-yield volatility, forcing central banks and the IMF to weigh harder policy trade-offs even as industrial competition (notably China–EU auto/EV rivalry) and NATO–Russia tensions reshape alliance politics and trade rules. The result is simultaneous stress across regional security complexes, global energy markets, financial markets and manufacturing supply chains, with spillovers accelerating and feedbacks hard to control.
system_description.scope: Interactions among states, non-state armed actors, energy and commodity markets, global financial markets and central banks, industrial supply chains and trade policy, major firms, and international organisations that connect security, markets and trade flows.
system_description.super_system: The broader globalised political-economic-technological system (world economy, international security architecture, and planetary resource/energy environment).
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East regional security complex (Iran, Saudi, Houthis, shipping through Hormuz)
Global energy and commodity markets (oil, diesel, LNG, shipping/freight)
Global financial-markets and central banking system (sovereign debt, bond yields, inflation)
Global industrial/trade subsystem (autos, EVs, China–EU–US competition and supply chains)

variables.name: Iran‑backed Houthi campaign
variables.description: Iran‑backed Houthi militants are intensifying missile, drone and missile‑strike operations against Saudi infrastructure and airports, escalating a regional military confrontation and diplomatic fallout.

variables.name: Russia–West military confrontation
variables.description: Russia’s sustained offensive in Ukraine, combined with strikes on critical infrastructure and escalating hybrid operations, is driving NATO and European militaries to deepen preparedness and strategic recalibration.

variables.name: China–Europe industrial and auto rivalry
variables.description: Chinese automakers and industrial champions are rapidly expanding into European markets while Beijing and Brussels negotiate caps, local‑content rules and other trade measures, shifting industrial competition and supply‑chain dynamics with knock‑on effects for broader Western policy.

variables.name: Global energy and diesel supply shock
variables.description: A mix of attacks on shipping and refineries, OPEC+ output dynamics and ad‑hoc cross‑border diesel arrangements involving major producers and consumers is tightening fuel markets and producing acute price and logistical volatility for global energy markets.

variables.name: Global financial stress and AI‑reshaping of growth
variables.description: Rising bond yields, sticky inflation and tighter central‑bank policy—combined with large, uneven AI investment—are reordering growth prospects, fiscal pressures and capital flows across major economies.
